steps.message: The build succeeds. Here is the final patch:

## Diagnosis

The defect is in `app/src/main/java/com/trianguloy/urlchecker/modules/list/UriPartsModule.java`, in `UriPartsDialog.onDisplayUrl()`.

The query was parsed like this:

```java
urlQuerySanitizer.parseQuery(uri.getQuery().replace("%", "%25"));
```

`Uri.getQuery()` returns the **already percent-decoded** query. So for `https://example.com/?q=a%26b%3Dc` it returns `q=a&b=c`. By the time `UrlQuerySanitizer.parseQuery()` splits on `&` and `=`, the encoded separators are indistinguishable from real ones, producing two bogus parameters (`q → a`, `b → c`). The `.replace("%", "%25")` hack only papered over the *double*-decoding of literal `%`, it couldn't recover the lost distinction between `%26`/`%3D` and `&`/`=`.

## Fix

Split the query while it is **still encoded**, and only decode each name/value afterwards:

- Use `uri.getEncodedQuery()` instead of `uri.getQuery()`.
- Replaced `UrlQuerySanitizer` (which forces decode-then-split and also mangles `+`/`%`) with a small `splitQuery()` helper that splits the encoded query on real `&`, then on the first real `=`, keeping `[name, value, raw]` triplets.
- Display values via `Uri.decode(...)`, so `q` now correctly shows `a&b=c`.
- The per-parameter delete button now rebuilds the URL with `encodedQuery(...)` by re-joining the untouched raw parameters, instead of re-encoding via `appendQueryParameter`. This preserves the original encoding of the remaining parameters exactly (previously, removing one parameter could rewrite the encoding of the others).
- Empty parameters (e.g. a trailing `&`) are skipped, matching the old row count behaviour.

## Verification

- Parsing logic checked against `q=a%26b%3Dc` → single param `q` = `a%26b%3Dc` (decodes to `a&b=c`), while `q=a&b=c` still yields two params; edge cases (`flag` with no `=`, trailing `&`, empty/null query, `%20%25` values) behave correctly.
- `./gradlew clean assembleDebug` → **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**.
